transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Yuki Tanaka (BlueCove CTO), Hana Sato (Head of Platform), Kenji Mori (DevOps), Ryo Nakamura (Security), Mika Kobayashi (Sourcing)

Summary (auto): Discussed renewal terms and path to onboard Japan edge pilot; covered capacity uplift, VPC/on‑prem constraints, security artifacts, and benchmarking. Agreed next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes, um, want to make sure we cover the renewal ask and the japan pilot that you sent over, Yuki?
[00:18] Yuki: yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. we, we are approaching our renewal window and we have two asks — short extension to cover the pilot and a capacity bump for peak Q4 traffic in APAC.
[00:30] Jordan: got it. what's the bump you are thinking about? is this sustained or burst?
[00:35] Hana: mostly sustained for customer-facing inference, but with spikes during certain campaign windows. baseline is about 2.2T tokens/day, want a 20% uplift and a 2x burst pool for 2 hours a day at peak.
[00:48] Priya: quick clarifying question — when you say burst pool, do you expect Redwood Dedicated or Hosted burst? there are different cost profiles.
[00:55] Kenji: preference is dedicated-ish for predictability, but security needs may push us to VPC/on-prem for the Japan edge pilot. if we can get predictable latency with dedicated plus VPC in region that would be ideal.
[01:10] Jordan: okay, so two parallel asks: billing/commit for uplift + burst, and a Japan-edge pilot that might be in our Private/VPC offering. we can propose a short 3-month bridge extension to keep current rates while pilot runs.
[01:25] Yuki: yes that bridge is what procurement wants so they don't have to renegotiate now. Mika from sourcing is here and can confirm.
[01:32] Mika: hi everyone — yes we want the flexibility. if the pilot shows measurable latency improvement we will convert to a longer term.
[01:40] Priya: noted. from the SE side, the biggest engineering work will be network (VPC peering/Transit) and KMS integration for keys on the edge nodes. do you plan to use your KMS or require Redwood-managed keys/HSM?
[01:55] Ryo: security flag — we prefer customer-managed keys in our HSM if possible, but open to Redwood-managed KMS for initial pilot. main ask is auditability and export control compliance for Japan data.
[02:10] Priya: okay, we can support customer KMS with a connector pattern; if HSM is required we'll need a few more steps (paperwork + SC). i'll capture that as an action.
[02:20] Kenji: also, curious about latency numbers — what are typical tail latencies for short prompts (<=128 tokens) in the tokyo region on Dedicated?
[02:30] Priya: ballpark on Dedicated in ap-northeast (tokyo) is 45-60ms p50 for short prompts, p95 120-180ms depending on model and kv cache hit rate; with our japan edge kernel selections we can squeeze p95 closer to 100ms in many cases. but real results depend on your seq len distro and batching.
[02:52] Yuki: ok that sounds promising. we'll provide traffic profile so you can simulate.
[03:00] Jordan: perfect — Kenji can you share the CSV of representative traffic (seq len distribution + tokens per request)? that helps Priya size batchers and kv cache.
[03:10] Kenji: yes i'll pull that and send today.
[03:13] Jordan: great. on pricing — Hana, do you have target budget range for the uplift and burst?
[03:20] Hana: ballpark we can expand 15-25% on committed spend this quarter; burst budget is limited so we'd prefer cost-on-burst with predictable cap.
[03:30] Jordan: okay we'll model two options — committed uplift + lower unit price, or smaller commit + larger burst credit pool. we'll show numbers in a revised quote.
[03:40] Mika: procurement will prefer the smaller commit + burst if total cost is within 10% of the committed model.
[03:48] Priya: noted, i'll include both in the worksheet.
[03:52] Ryo: one more on security: SOC2 report timing — BlueCove requires a SOC2 Type II in the contract annex, do you have that?
[04:01] Jordan: Redwood has SOC2 Type II completed earlier this year — i'll attach the latest report and the controls mapping. also can include KMS/HSM design docs.
[04:10] Ryo: please include encryption at rest specifics for edge nodes and how audit logs are retained; data residency controls for Japan.
[04:18] Priya: for edge we have options: replicate logs to customer's SIEM over secure channel or provide Redwood-hosted long term retention with RBAC. we'll note both.
[04:28] Yuki: excellent. timeline wise procurement wants to sign the short extension by end of month so the pilot can start early November. is that workable?
[04:36] Jordan: yes, if we turn around quote and SOW within 3 business days we can do a fast contract amendment for the 3-month bridge.
[04:45] Hana: and then pilot run would be 4 weeks with telemetry, after which we'd decide to convert.
[04:50] Priya: for pilot instrumentation we'll want a small set of prompt/traffic tests, plus an A/B baseline to your existing hosted infra. the benchmark window should be non‑production but realistic.
[05:02] Kenji: sounds good. what about rollback/fallback if edge nodes are unhealthy? we need autoswitch to a fallback region.
[05:10] Jordan: automatic fallback is supported — routing policy can failover to a compatible model in another region; we'll include the failover SLAs in the SOW.
[05:20] Ryo: any concerns about egress or transfer pricing for cross-region fallbacks?
[05:25] Jordan: we'll surface egress assumptions in the quote; we can also propose local-only data routing to minimize that.
[05:32] Yuki: ok let's talk about the benchmarking schedule now — next Thursday morning JST would work for our engineers.
[05:39] Priya: we have an SE-run slot Thurs 02:00 UTC which is 11:00 JST — would that fit?
[05:45] Kenji: yes that's ideal.
[05:48] Jordan: i'll send an invite. action items recap in a bit. any objections on the short 3-month extension?
[05:55] Mika: procurement aligns, yes. we just need final SOW and security appendix.
[06:00] Jordan: great. one more note on model variants — if you want lower cost we can suggest smaller quantized variants for non-critical flows during bursts.
[06:10] Hana: show that in the worksheet, please. interesting if quantized path keeps quality.
[06:15] Priya: we have some evals that show minimal quality delta for retrieval/light-turn prompts; i'll include a short note and examples.
[06:22] Yuki: that helps our finance review.
[06:25] Jordan: ok let's do a short recap and next steps.
[06:28] Jordan: recap: Redwood will send updated quote (two pricing options), SOW for 3-month bridge extension, SOC2 and KMS/HSM docs; SE will produce pilot runbook and benchmark plan; BlueCove will send traffic profile and security artifact list; schedule benchmark for next Thurs 11:00 JST.
[06:46] Yuki: thanks, that matches.
[06:48] Hana: thanks everyone.
[06:50] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and attach the docs.

End of transcript.

References shared: SOW template (link: drive.redwood/sow-templates/edge-pilot.pdf), pricing worksheet (link: drive.redwood/pricing/bluecove-q4-uplift.xlsx), SOC2 report (redwood-sec/soc2-2026.pdf)
